### Changed
- **Blue is back.** The greys from 2.0.0 are blues again: night-blue pages, cards and popups under a still navy wash at the top, a solid blue main button, and a lighter blue for progress, links, selections and switches. The app icon and the logo tiles have their colour back, in a brighter blue than before 2.0.0. The Live Activities and sideinstaller.net match.

detail.readme:
# SideInstaller **Install SideStore and LiveContainer directly on your iPhone. No PC required.** [![Install](https://img.shields.io/badge/Install-SideInstaller-2ea44f?style=for-the-badge)](https://sideinstaller.net/) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.0.1-2669ed?style=for-the-badge)](CHANGELOG.md) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-iOS-lightgrey?style=for-the-badge&logo=apple)](#requirements) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Custom-orange?style=for-the-badge)](LICENSE.md)
--- > [!CAUTION] > **Only install SideInstaller from the official source.** > > This project is open source, which means anyone can fork the code, insert a credential stealer that > uploads your Apple ID and password to their own server, rebuild it, and redistribute it under the same > name and icon. A malicious fork looks identical to the real app from the outside. > > The **only** builds I publish are: > - **Website:** https://sideinstaller.net/ > - **Repository:** https://github.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller > > Do not install SideInstaller from any other site, AltStore source, Telegram channel, Discord server, > app repo, or mirror, no matter how official it looks. Redistributing my builds without explicit consent is also prohibited by > the [license](LICENSE.md). > > There is a fake site called “sideinstaller.com”. This site is **not legit**, and is likely providing malware. Please make sure > you only download from the **official sources** listed above. --- ## What it is SideStore and LiveContainer are currently the best way to sideload on iOS. However, there's one big problem: installing them requires a PC, which many people don't have. That's why I made SideInstaller, a free and open-source iOS app that installs them directly on your iPhone, no PC required. SideInstaller handles the entire setup process on-device. It takes care of the pairing, provisioning, and installation steps that normally force you to plug into a computer and run desktop tools, all from a single app running on the phone itself. Once it's done, you get a fully working SideStore and LiveContainer setup ready to sideload your own apps. The whole thing is built to be simple. There's no complicated configuration, no command line, and no need to understand how any of the underlying machinery works. You just open the app, follow a few steps, and let it do the rest. For anyone who's ever wanted to sideload but didn't own a Mac or PC, this removes the biggest barrier to getting started. And because it's open source, you don't have to take my word for any of it. The full code is available for anyone to read, audit, or contribute to, so you can see exactly what's running on your device. ## Requirements - An iPhone or iPad on iOS 27+ (iOS 17.4+ with a pairing file made on a computer; from iOS 26.4, a [remote pairing one](#ios-264-to-26x-a-remote-pairing-file)) - Wi-Fi (first time only) - Your Apple account credentials (not collected) ## How to use it [siboot](https://github.com/FrizzleM/siboot) installs SideInstaller from the iPhone itself, signed with your own Apple account: no computer and no certificate. You need iOS 27 or later, Wi-Fi and Developer Mode on. [sideinstaller.net](https://sideinstaller.net/) shows steps 1 to 3. 1. **Get the apps.** Install [rootshell](https://apps.apple.com/app/rootshell-local-terminal-ssh/id6755794662), [Open Minis](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6759188481) and [LocalDevVPN](https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755608044), all free on the App Store. 2. **Pair in rootshell.** Turn on **Settings › Location Diary Mode › Session Only** in rootshell, then tap **Local Shell** and **Open** at the top right, and run these one line at a time: ```sh curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FrizzleM/siboot/main/rootshell/bin/siboot-pair.wasm ifconfig en0 > ifconfig.txt ./siboot-pair.wasm ``` Open **Settings › Privacy & Security › Developer Mode**, scroll to the bottom, tap **Pair with siboot**, and enter your passcode and the code rootshell shows. Leave rootshell running. 3. **Install from Open Minis.** Connect LocalDevVPN. In Open Minis, tap the console icon at the top right, then **Shell Terminal**, and run: ```sh wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FrizzleM/siboot/main/minis/install.sh | sh ``` Type the transfer code rootshell shows (only the first time: after that, siboot uses the pairing file it saved), then your Apple account email, password and verification code. Keep Minis open until it says it's done. The first time, trust your Apple account in **Settings › General › VPN & Device Management**. 4. **Open SideInstaller.** With LocalDevVPN connected, log in with your Apple account and tap **Install SideStore** or **Install SideStore + LiveContainer**. Once paired, `siboot developer-mode` in Open Minis asks the iPhone to show the Developer Mode switch in Settings, or with `--turn-on` to turn it on ([details](https://github.com/FrizzleM/siboot/blob/main/minis/README.md#developer-mode)). ### Legacy: enterprise certificates Before iOS 27, or if siboot doesn't work for you, install SideInstaller with one of the enterprise certificates at [sideinstaller.net/#legacy](https://sideinstaller.net/#legacy) instead, then go on from step 4. ### Links SideInstaller opens three kinds of `sideinstaller://` link, and asks before acting on any of them: - `sideinstaller://install?url=` downloads the IPA as the custom .ipa and installs it, for one-tap installs from a website. - `sideinstaller://pairingFile?data=` imports a pairing file. SideStore sends one back when asked with `sidestore://pairing?urlname=sideinstaller`, which is what **Get it from SideStore** on the Pairing file card does. - `sideinstaller://certificate?data=&password=` makes SideInstaller sign with that certificate from then on, once Apple lists it among your Apple ID's certificates. **Use SideStore's certificate** (on the “A certificate already exists” popup and the Certificates page) asks SideStore for its own with `sidestore://certificate?callback_template=sideinstaller://certificate?data=$(BASE64_CERT)&password=$(PASSWORD)` (percent-encoded), so a free Apple ID's one certificate serves both apps. That reply is the one link that doesn't ask again: SideStore has just asked whether to export it. Discord and most chat apps only make `https://` links tappable, so to post an install link there use `https://sideinstaller.net/open.html?url=`. That page shows where the IPA downloads from and hands it to `sideinstaller://install`, with a button for when iOS doesn't open the app on its own. ## Compatibility | iOS | Is it compatible? | | --- | --- | | 27+ | ✅ Yes | | 26.4 - 26.7 | ⚠️ Yes, but [a remote pairing file is needed](#ios-264-to-26x-a-remote-pairing-file), and that requires a PC | | 17.4 - 26.3 | ⚠️ Yes, but [a pairing file is needed](https://docs.sidestore.io/docs/advanced/alternative#pairing), and that requires a PC | | <17.4 | ❌ No | ### iOS 26.4 to 26.x: a remote pairing file Since iOS 26.4, the iPhone hangs up on lockdown pairing files (from jitterbugpair, `pymobiledevice3 lockdown pair`, or idevice_pair's **Lockdown**) as soon as they connect through LocalDevVPN, so they can't be used on the iPhone any more, however new. A remote pairing (RPPairing) file still works: 1. On a Mac, Windows PC or Linux computer, open [idevice_pair](https://github.com/jkcoxson/idevice_pair/releases/latest) and plug the iPhone in. Tap **Trust** if it asks. 2. Pick the iPhone, choose **Remote pairing**, click **Create**, and keep the iPhone unlocked until it's done. 3. Click **Save to file…** and send the file to the iPhone by AirDrop, iCloud Drive or a cable. 4. In SideInstaller, tap **Import pairing file** (or **Replace**) and pick it. A pairing file exported from [iLoader](https://github.com/nab138/iloader) (**Manage Pairing File** › **Export**) holds both kinds and works too. ## Is SideInstaller safe? SideInstaller is built with safety and privacy in mind. The app is fully local and open source, which means anyone can inspect exactly what it does. **Your Apple credentials never leave your device.** They're used locally, only to sign and install your apps, and are never transmitted, logged, or collected in any way. **No server, no analytics, no account.** Nothing is collected and there's nothing to sign up for. **Fully auditable.** Every line of it can be verified in the source code. > [!WARNING] > All of the above is true of **this** repository and the builds published from it. It is **not** a guarantee > that applies to forks, re-signed IPAs, or copies you find elsewhere, those can be modified to steal the > Apple ID you type into them. If you didn't get it from > https://sideinstaller.net/, don't trust it with your > credentials. ## Project layout | Path | What's in it | | :-- | :-- | | `ios-app/` | The SwiftUI app — UI, install engine, certificate handling, translations | | `ios-live-activity/` | The widget extension that draws the pairing code in the Dynamic Island and on the Lock Screen | | `ios-tests/` | The app's unit tests (`SideInstallerTests`) | | `rust-core/` | Rust core compiled into `SideInstallerFFI.xcframework` | | `scripts/` | Build, check and release scripts | | `.github/` | Workflows that check pull requests, build the unsigned IPA, publish it as a release and hand it to the signer | Signed builds and the install page live in [FrizzleM/SideInstaller-Signed](https://github.com/FrizzleM/SideInstaller-Signed): it signs each release's IPA with every certificate, attaches the signed IPAs to a release of its own and deploys [sideinstaller.net](https://sideinstaller.net/). No IPA is ever committed to either repository. siboot, which installs SideInstaller [from the iPhone itself](#how-to-use-it), lives in [FrizzleM/siboot](https://github.com/FrizzleM/siboot). It builds this repository's vendored crates and rust-core's `apple_session.rs` and `error_text.rs` through a submodule pinned to one commit, so a change here reaches siboot only when that pin moves. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. If you're reporting a bug, please include your iOS version, the app version, and the step where it failed. Every pull request is checked by the `checks` workflow: the Rust tests and clippy, a simulator build with the app's unit tests, and the translations (a string added to the app needs an entry in each `ios-app/*Strings.swift`). The same checks run on a Mac with `scripts/test-rust.sh`, `scripts/check-ios.sh` (in a clean clone, since it generates the Xcode project) and `scripts/check_translations.py`. ## License See [LICENSE.md](LICENSE.md). In short: you may read, modify, and share the **source**, with attribution, for non-commercial purposes. Redistributing the official builds (IPAs) or monetizing the project in any form requires written permission.
